newsitem.title: USA: Aetna's Q2 HMO earnings rise.
newsitem.headline: Aetna's Q2 HMO earnings rise.

text.p: Aetna Inc said on Tuesday its Aetna U.S. Healthcare operation's second quarter operating earnings rose 29 percent over last year's pro forma results, excluding the effects of goodwill amortization and unusual items.

Aetna U.S. Healthcare, which provides managed care, indemnity and group insurance products and services, reported $152 million in second quarter operating earnings, after $74.6 million in after-tax goodwill amortization.

Second quarter 1997 earnings include a $20.2 million after-tax benefit from a reduction in the severance and facilities reserve as the integration of the U.S. Healthcare acquisition proceeded at less cost than initially expected.
Second quarter operating earnings in 1996, which do not reflect U.S. Healthcare results, were $81.0 million, excluding a severance and facilities charge unrelated to the merger.

Aetna said Aetna U.S. Healthcare's sales, general and administrative expenses fell eight percent from a year ago on a pro forma basis as the business continued to focus on lowering its cost structure.

Operating earnings from the Health Risk business, which includes those products in which the company assumes all or a majority of health care cost and utilization risk, decreased from the year ago period on a pro forma basis, Aetna said.
The results were hurt by increases in commercial and Medicare HMO medical costs, Aetna said.
Medical costs were higher than prior-year periods as higher inpatient, physician and pharmacy costs were only partially slowed by recontracting and intensified patient management efforts, Aetna said.

However, commercial HMO enrollment grew by 10 percent over the second quarter of 1996 on a pro forma basis and Medicare risk membership grew 32 percent over 1996's second quarter on a pro forma basis, Aetna said.
Overall Medicare membership grew by 21,000 members from the first quarter and stood at 369,000 at June 30, 1997.
Operating earnings for the group insurance and other health businesses nearly doubled over 1996's second quarter on a pro forma basis, Aetna said.
Fee increases in the health portion of the business and lower operating expenses were major contributors.
Aetna Retirement Services reported second quarter 1997 operating earnings of $56.5 million, up 21 percent from a year ago.
Aetna International reported second quarter 1997 operating earnings of $32.2 million, up 19 percent from a year ago.
Large Case Pensions reported second quarter 1997 operating earnings of $28.1 million.
In the second quarter of 1996, Large Case Pensions had $25.7 million in operating earnings, excluding a $110.5 million benefit from the reduction in reserves for discontinued products.

This nine percent increase in earnings was primarily due to favorable mortality reserve developments and lower operating expenses, which were partially offset by lower income on the capital supporting this business in the second quarter, Aetna said.

The corporate segment reported net operating expenses of $63.0 million for the second quarter of 1997, compared with $14.3 million for the second quarter of 1996, which excludes a $236.0 million after-tax severance and facilities charge related to the sale of the company's property-casualty business, Aetna said.
The second quarter of 1997 also reflects $21.0 million of increased interest expense primarily related to debt incurred in connection with the U.S. Healthcare merger.
Also, the 1996 second quarter included $30.0 million of investment income on the proceeds received from the property-casualty sale.
